title: Humanlike AI Design Increases Anthropomorphism but Yields Divergent Outcomes on Engagement and Trust Globally
findings: The paper posits that religious traditions can be a significant cultural factor influencing AI anthropomorphism. It cites 'Japanese culture and religious traditions that attribute spirit to non-human objects' and 'Buddhist funeral ceremonies for Sony’s AIBO robots' as examples of worldviews that may predispose individuals to be more open to anthropomorphizing AI. While data on religion was collected, the primary analysis focused on broader country-level cultural differences rather than specific religious effects.
